claim: PARIPRASHNA_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE_v0_1 §14A.3: 'Cloud SQL automated backups may be enabled at the instance level; nothing in-repo verifies or documents that, which means nobody knows.'
reality: Verified live via gcloud: Cloud SQL PITR is DISABLED on the production instance amjis-postgres (pointInTimeRecoveryEnabled=False). Daily automated backups ARE enabled (backupTier=STANDARD, backupRetentionSettings={'retainedBackups': 7, 'retentionUnit': 'COUNT'}, startTime=02:00, transactionLogRetentionDays=7) but transactionalLogStorageState is UNSPECIFIED and replicationLogArchivingEnabled=False, consistent with PITR being off (log archiving for PITR is not running). This means restore is limited to the 7 most recent daily snapshot backups, NOT to an arbitrary point in time within a retention window. The architecture doc's own recommended remediation ('Verify and document the Cloud SQL backup configuration — PITR window, retention, and where it lives. First action, costs an hour.') has never been executed; this audit is the first verification on record.

evidence.quote: Verified: no scheduled backup job, no restore script, no PITR/RPO/RTO documentation, no DR runbook in the repo. ... Cloud SQL automated backups may be enabled at the instance level; nothing in-repo verifies or documents that, which means nobody knows.

recommended_action: Enable PITR (pointInTimeRecoveryEnabled=true) on amjis-postgres with a documented retention window (doc recommends near-zero RPO for conversation_messages/message_parts + prediction ledger); state the RPO/RTO explicitly in-repo per §14A.3's fourth bullet. Current posture only protects against total data loss back to the last of 7 daily snapshots, not point-in-time recovery for mid-day incidents (e.g. bad migration, accidental delete during a session).

claim: §14A.3: 'A restore runbook that has actually been executed once against a scratch instance. An untested backup is a belief, not a backup.' — implies no restore has ever been tested.
reality: Confirmed still true. Repo-wide grep for restore-drill/runbook language found no DR/PITR restore rehearsal against a scratch Cloud SQL instance. The only 'restore' hits in the corpus are: (1) BA_BRIEF_PACK_P2_P7_v1_0.md's exit-gate checklist item 'rollback tested = ⟦snapshot⟧ restore rehearsed on Abhinandan' — an unfilled template slot (⟦snapshot⟧), not a completed/dated rehearsal record; (2) MARSYS_DEFECT_GAP_REGISTER_v2_0.md's Y-13 finding describing an application-level chart-table restore-from-snapshot during a guarded rebuild on 2026-07-11 — that is a per-chart data-repair action (delete-then-insert idempotent rebuild recovery per CLAUDE.md §N.3), not a Cloud SQL infrastructure-level backup/PITR restore drill. 7 successful daily backups exist per `gcloud sql backups list` but a backup existing is not the same as a tested restore path.

evidence.quote: bodha_contradictions > 0 both charts; rollback tested = ⟦snapshot⟧ restore rehearsed on Abhinandan.
halted, chart restored from snapshot per native's no-iteration-on-native-chart instruction

recommended_action: Execute one real Cloud SQL restore-to-scratch-instance drill (from an existing daily backup) and record the runbook + timing (actual RTO) in-repo, per §14A.3's second bullet. This is distinct from and does not depend on enabling PITR (PG1-O1-0001).

claim: CONDUCTOR_PROTOCOL.md §8.3/§8.4 describes deploy as: not push-triggered, gated on 'CI — Ganga Quality Gate' passing on main, then deploy.yml fires via workflow_run; deploy no-traffic → smoke → promote traffic; emergency path via workflow_dispatch (bypasses CI); rollback via `gcloud run services update-traffic <service> --to-revisions <prev-revision>=100`.
reality: Matches the live .github/workflows/deploy.yml exactly. The workflow triggers on `workflow_run` for workflows: ["CI — Ganga Quality Gate"] on branches [main], plus `pull_request` (build-check only, no push/deploy) and `workflow_dispatch` (emergency bypass). Web deploy job guards `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`, deploys amjis-web with `--no-traffic`, runs `scripts/operator/end_to_end_smoke.sh` as a named 'Post-deploy smoke' step, then 'Promote traffic to latest revision' via `gcloud run services update-traffic amjis-web ...`. amjis-mcp and the pipeline job follow the same gated pattern, path-filtered via a `changes` job.

# ── A-S8: Deploy no-traffic, smoke, then promote ──────────────────────────
- name: Promote traffic to latest revision

recommended_action: None — documentation and implementation are in sync. No action needed.

claim: PARIPRASHNA_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE §19 P1' (and D-17's disposable-shim sequencing) assumes a route/behavior can be flag-gated during rollout.
reality: Confirmed: the codebase already has a working env-var feature-flag system, not a stub. `platform/src/lib/config/feature_flags.ts` defines `DEFAULT_FLAGS`/`FLAG_ENV_PREFIX`/`FeatureFlag` type, consumed by `platform/src/lib/config/index.ts`. deploy.yml bakes ~10 flags into the Next.js build as `NEXT_PUBLIC_MARSYS_FLAG_*` build-args (e.g. R9_PERSONAS, R10_SCROLL_DISCIPLINE, R10_EDIT_WHILE_STREAMING=false, R11C_TOOL_CARDS), meaning flags are already used to gate shipped-but-off functionality per release. Separately there is a DB-driven `gate_registry.ts` with a `feature_flag` gate class (`platform/src/lib/gates/gate_registry.ts`) used for kill-switches (e.g. `/api/build/start` feature-flag kill-switch tests) and Observatory route guards (403 when flag disabled). No LaunchDarkly-style dynamic remote-config system was found — flags are compile-time env-vars (Next.js `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`, requiring a rebuild+redeploy to flip) plus a separate DB-backed runtime gate class for server-side kill-switches.
recommended_action: P1' shim work can rely on the existing NEXT_PUBLIC_MARSYS_FLAG_* env-var pattern for build-time gating; if the shim needs a runtime (no-redeploy) kill-switch, use the existing DB-backed gate_registry.ts feature_flag class rather than building a third mechanism.

claim: §1.1 A-27: 'Accessibility is preserved and extended, not added — the current aria-live-while-streaming pattern is correct and must survive the renderer rebuild.'
reality: Confirmed live in the current codebase (pre-rebuild baseline the assumption is measured against). `platform/src/components/chat/MarkdownContent.tsx:172` sets `aria-live={streaming ? 'polite' : 'off'}`; `platform/src/components/chat/ReasoningProgress.tsx:274` sets `aria-live={isStreaming ? 'polite' : undefined}`. A behavioral test asserts this contract: `platform/src/components/consume/__tests__/co6_behavioral.test.tsx:144` ('has aria-live="polite" when streaming'). The assumption accurately describes the pattern to be preserved; no axe-core harness integration was found yet (that is the A-27 forward-looking ask, not yet built), which is expected since A-27 is a design conclusion for the rebuild, not a claim that axe-core already exists.
recommended_action: None for the assumption itself (accurately grounded). Track axe-core harness integration as still-outstanding forward work under §12.12, not yet present in the repo.

claim: §1.1 A-28: 'Cross-conversation, per-chart memory, with prior_reading as its own citation kind that can never satisfy an acharya-floor requirement.'
reality: This is correctly framed as a forward design conclusion, not a claim about current state — and the repo confirms it does not exist yet. Grep for `prior_reading` across platform/src and platform-mcp/src returns zero hits; no cross-conversation/per-chart memory citation-kind implementation was found. The only related infrastructure is generic session/chat history within a single conversation (conversation_messages/message_parts per D-16), not a cross-conversation retrieval mechanism. This is consistent with the document's own framing (§1.1 preamble: 'These are not native rulings but design conclusions... open to challenge') — A-28 is unbuilt by design, so class 'partial' here reflects that the assumption is honest about its own not-yet-built status, not a discrepancy to fix.
recommended_action: No correction needed to the document. When A-28 moves from design conclusion to implementation, this finding should be re-run to confirm prior_reading citation-kind and its acharya-floor exclusion are actually implemented as specified.
